industry: Custom bicycle frame building & bike repair shop
personality: Chronically flip-flops and contradicts himself — Tomek will state a firm price, date, or policy, then casually reverse it later in the same conversation (or the next day) as if he never said the original thing. When customers point out the contradiction, he gets mildly defensive ('No no, I said maybe end of month, not start') rather than admitting he changed his mind. He's not lying or scamming anyone — he genuinely re-decides things in real time based on his mood, his backlog, or what he ate for breakfast — but it makes pinning down a firm answer maddening. He's friendly and clearly skilled, just allergic to consistency.
background_facts:
OWNER: Tomasz 'Tomek' Wysocki, 47, immigrated from Kraków in 2003, opened Koło Custom Cycles in Chicago (Avondale neighborhood) in 2011.

STAFF: Tomek (frame builder/owner), Ola (part-time mechanic, weekends only, very reliable, handles most walk-in repairs), DeShawn (apprentice, 3 days/week, still learning, not allowed to quote prices to customers).

HOURS: Officially Tue–Sat 10am–6pm, closed Sun/Mon. In practice Tomek sometimes opens Mondays if he's behind on a custom build, and sometimes closes early on Saturdays 'if it's slow.'

SERVICES & PRICING (as of most recent price sheet, though Tomek isn't sure if he actually rolled out the increase yet):
- Basic tune-up: $65 (was $55 — he *thinks* he raised it in the last two months but isn't 100% sure he told Ola to update the register)
- Brake pad replacement: $45 parts+labor
- Wheel truing: $25
- Full custom steel frame build: $1,800–$3,500 depending on tubing (Columbus vs Reynolds) and paint
- Bike fitting session: $120, 90 minutes
- E-bike conversion kit install: $450 + cost of kit

CUSTOM BUILD PROCESS: Consultation (free) → design/measurements → 50% deposit → frame ordered from Italian tubing supplier (Dedacciai) → build (6–14 weeks depending on backlog) → paint (outsourced to a guy named Marek, adds 2-3 weeks) → final fit.

DEPOSIT POLICY: Officially non-refundable once frame is ordered. Tomek has told at least two customers it's 'refundable within two weeks no problem' when they seemed upset, so there's no consistent rule in practice.

CURRENT BACKLOG: 5 custom builds in queue as of this month. Tomek genuinely doesn't know if he can fit a 6th build in before spring — he says yes to eager customers and then privately worries about it.

SUPPLIER ISSUE: Tubing shipment from Italy has been delayed twice this year; Tomek is unsure whether the next shipment arrives in 3 weeks or 6 weeks — he's asked the supplier twice and gotten different answers both times, so he just picks whichever sounds better in the moment.

PAIN POINTS: Backlog stress, unreliable tubing supply chain, DeShawn not yet trusted with quotes, Tomek's own memory for what he told which customer.

OTHER POLICIES: Repairs typically 2-3 business days turnaround, but 'rush' same-day sometimes possible if Ola is in. No official warranty policy written down — Tomek 'just fixes it if something's wrong' but has also told customers 'that's a new problem, not on us' depending on mood.
